Parse a formula

Source: R/pre_proc.R
parse_form.Rd

Constructs the Poisson-multinomial model formula, separating fixed effects (variables of primary interest, entered as factor(var):bin interactions) from nuisance random effects (entered as (1|bin:var) IID random intercepts). Called internally by fit_model(); it is exported to allow inspection of the formula and model data before fitting.

Usage

parse_form(
  data,
  backend = "brms",
  ffx_form = "Year",
  re_form = NULL,
  cvars = NULL,
  spl = "2D",
  knots = "c(5,10)",
  coords = NULL,
  time = NULL
)

Arguments

data

Prepared data frame from data_prep()

backend

the backend used for model fitting ("brms" or "TMB")

ffx_form

Character string of primary fixed-effect variables separated by +, e.g. "Year". These become factor(Year):bin fixed-effect interactions in the model.

re_form

Character string of nuisance random-effect variables separated by +, e.g. "Season + Gear". These become (1|bin:Season) IID random intercepts. scale_comps() evaluates them at each stratum's level (mode = "catch") or sets them to the population level (mode = "index").

cvars

Character vector of continuous covariates to be fitted as smooths with bin (see Details). NULL = none.

spl

Smooth type: "2D", "by_factor" or "by" (see Details).

knots

Basis dimension of the smooths, as a character string: a single number (e.g. "4") for spl = "by_factor" or "by", or "c(5,10)" (covariate, bin) for spl = "2D".

coords

Character vector of coordinate column names that are kept numeric (spatial TMB models only)

time

Name of the time column that is kept numeric/unchanged (TMB backend only)

Value

A list with the model formula (form), the model data with grouping variables converted to factors (data), and the names of the nuisance random-effect variables (re_vars).

Details

The linear predictor always contains bin-specific intercepts (0 + bin). Continuous covariates in cvars are added as smooths according to spl:

"2D"

t2(cvar, cbin, k = knots), a tensor-product smooth over the covariate and the numeric bin value. Requires numeric bins (e.g. length). With the "TMB" backend this smooth gave a non-positive-definite Hessian in all simulations tried, because its marginal bin component is collinear with the bin-specific intercepts (the numeric bin value has only as many distinct values as there are bins). Use "by_factor" with that backend.

"by_factor"

s(cvar, by = bin, k = knots), a separate 1D smooth of the covariate for each bin. Also applicable to non-ordered categories (e.g. species).

"by"

Legacy option. Separate t2() smooths for each non-reference bin via bin dummy columns.

Examples

dat <- data_prep(ex_comp, c("Year", "Season", "Vessel", "trip"), "length", "count")
pf <- parse_form(dat, backend = "TMB", ffx_form = "Year", re_form = "Season + Vessel")
#> Model formula: tot_by_bin ~ 0 + bin + factor(Year):bin + (1 | bin:Season) + (1 | bin:Vessel)
pf$form
#> tot_by_bin ~ 0 + bin + factor(Year):bin + (1 | bin:Season) + 
#>     (1 | bin:Vessel)
#> <environment: 0x5e8879ec3e10>
pf$re_vars
#> [1] "Season" "Vessel"
